proposals.old_pdf_text: the replay set contains previously seen relevant and irrelevant tasks:
proposals.old_source_text: For each skill, the replay set contains previously seen relevant and irrelevant tasks:
proposals.proposed_text_or_action: For each skill s, retain at most N relevant and N irrelevant historical tasks. Score candidates on the union of these buckets and the current failed task, de-duplicated by task identifier; this set contains at most 2N+1 tasks. The per-skill replay sets are bounded, but the global seen-task history used for lazy bucket materialization is not. Our default uses N=5, three generated replacements, and a 400-character predicate limit. After each full training pass, validation admission is checked against the initial predicate; rejection or absent validation support restores the iteration-start predicate.
conditional_inputs: Author approval; confirmation that Appendix A.2/D.1 describes the evaluated runs
acceptance_criteria: Main and appendix define the same current-inclusive replay set and 2N+1 bound.
No passage implies bounded total history storage.
The main method states default replay capacity, proposal count and character limit.
Gate timing and rollback state agree with A.4; no previous-policy comparator is substituted for the initial-predicate comparator.

proposals.proposed_text_or_action: For ranked output, we order candidates first by the binary selection label (selected first), then by descending retrieval score, and finally by original retrieval order. The top-k variant returns the first k skills in this ordering and can include predicate-negative candidates; strict routing returns only selected skills.
conditional_inputs: Author confirmation that the documented lexicographic adapter applies to each reported baseline/retriever, not just RouterBSI

narrative_arc.thesis_sentence: Explicit, editable natural-language skill-applicability predicates can be improved from labeled routing failures using bounded per-skill replay selection and a cold-start held-out gate, while keeping model weights fixed.

contribution_ladder.contribution: We propose RouterBSI, a non-parametric skill-routing framework that evaluates explicit applicability predicates over retrieved candidates, making routing criteria interpretable and directly editable without updating the underlying language model.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Explicit natural-language predicate interface and concrete examples.

contribution_ladder.contribution: We develop a recursive self-improvement procedure that refines predicates from routing failures, selects updates through minimum Bayes risk over a bounded replay of relevant and irrelevant tasks, and rejects updates with higher held-out validation error than the cold-start predicate.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Minimum-average-risk equation, initial-predicate gate and four component configurations.

contribution_ladder.contribution: We evaluate RouterBSI on six SRA-Bench datasets with a shared 26K-skill corpus, achieving the highest aggregate nDCG@10 and Hit@1 among evaluated methods while ablations establish the contributions of replay and validation.
contribution_ladder.evidenced_by: Table 1 aggregate nDCG@1/nDCG@10; Figures 3,5–7 and detailed tables.
